# HAND-WRITTEN rows of the Minecraft 1.21.1 -> 26.2 rename table.
# This is NOT the whole table. A mod's versions/26.2.renames.tsv is COMPOSED by
# tools/make-multiversion.sh (via tools/compose-renames.py) from three sources:
#   1. this file -- rules a generator cannot derive: renamed types, call-shape regexes, and
#      the GeckoLib 4 -> 5 and NeoForge package moves;
#   2. $MIGRATE_WORKSPACE/moves/moves-1.21.1-to-26.2.tsv -- the class-move map, built by
#      tools/build-class-move-map.py from your two compile classpaths;
#   3. $MIGRATE_WORKSPACE/moves/colors-1.21.1-to-26.2.tsv -- the per-colour ColorCollection
#      rows, built by tools/gen-color-renames.py from the same classpaths.
# (2) and (3) are derived from Mojang's own names, so they are generated on your machine rather
# than published here. Anyone who needs them is already building both versions.
# SHARED starting table: Minecraft 1.21.1 -> 26.2 mechanical renames.
# Every rule here is a claim that the API is IDENTICAL either side -- only the NAME changed --
# and each was verified against the real 26.2 compile classpath while porting a 458-file mod to
# green on both targets. Copy it into <mod>/versions/26.2.renames.tsv and start from it rather
# than rediscovering the same 800 rows: on that port these closed the large majority of a
# 2254-error burn-down before any hand work began.
# THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE EDITING (the long form is CLAUDE.md section X):
#   * Order matters and getting it wrong is SILENT -- regex rules run before token rules, and
#     token rules longest-key-first. A regex anchored on a name a token rule produces can never
#     fire.
#   * A member rename must name its OWNER unless the member name is globally unique.
#     `MobEffects.MOVEMENT_SPEED` became SPEED; `Attributes.MOVEMENT_SPEED` did not.
#   * `prepare-sources.py` reports every rule that matched NOTHING. Drive that to zero and keep
#     it there, marking a genuinely-unused block `#!exhaustive` ... `#!strict` WITH A REASON.
#     A warning that is never zero is decoration.
# Rows carrying a judgement rather than a pure rename are commented as such -- keep those notes,
# because a compile cannot tell a faithful mapping from a merely plausible one.
# Mod-specific rows (compat-helper routing, a mod's own registry names) were stripped when this
# was promoted from that port: 15 of them. Yours go in your own table, not here.
# Mechanical 1.21.1 -> 26.2 renames applied to the shared tree by tools/prepare-sources.py.
# Every row is a type whose NAME or PACKAGE changed while its API stayed the same, so the
# rewrite is safe and reviewable. Rows come from diffing the two real compile classpaths
# (tools/build-class-move-map.py), not from memory.
# A change that is NOT a pure rename does not belong here -- it belongs in the target's
# overlay (src/mc26/java), which replaces a whole file.
# format: <1.21.1 name><TAB><26.2 name>
# -- the type rename with the widest blast radius. Identical statics
# -- (fromNamespaceAndPath/parse/withDefaultNamespace/tryParse/getNamespace/getPath),
# -- so call sites are untouched. FQN first for the import line, then the bare name.
#!exhaustive  # THE WHOLE INHERITED SWEEP IS EXEMPT, as one block.
#             # These rows were promoted from a 458-file port, so any given mod uses a
#             # fraction of them and the rest are dead BY DESIGN here -- a permanently
#             # large dead-rule count would train you to ignore the number that has to
#             # stay zero. Note there is deliberately no inner '#!strict': one would
#             # close this block early and re-arm the noise (X11).
#             # YOUR MOD'S OWN ROWS GO AFTER THE '#!strict' AT THE END OF THIS FILE,
#             # where a dead rule IS a real bug.
net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation
ResourceLocation

# -- (per-colour -> ColorCollection rows: GENERATED on your machine by tools/gen-color-renames.py
# --  from the game's own field names, and inserted by the composer -- see the header.)
# -- method renames, each resolved with javap against the real 26.2 classpath.
# ⚠ These were `member:` rules, which fire on a FIELD read too. Every one is a METHOD, so
#   each was one same-named field away from silently rewriting it -- which is exactly what
#   `member:location` did to a mod's own `this.location` (see the note above it). Requiring
#   the parentheses costs a method rename nothing and removes the whole class.
re:\.registryOrThrow\(
# Entity placement: moveTo -> snapTo.  MEASURED, and it is the OPPOSITE of what the
# name suggests -- 26.2 renamed BOTH families in lockstep:
#     moveTo    (5 overloads: double x3, +yaw/pitch, BlockPos, Vec3)  ->  snapTo
#     absMoveTo (2 overloads: doubles only)                           ->  absSnapTo
#     absRotateTo                                                     ->  absSnapRotationTo
# 1.21.1's moveTo(x,y,z,yRot,xRot) body is byte-for-byte 26.2's snapTo(...): setPosRaw,
# setYRot/setXRot, setOldPosAndRot, reapplyPosition.  absSnapTo is NOT that -- it clamps
# to the +/-3e7 world border and goes through setPos().  Mapping moveTo->absSnapTo compiles
# at every double-argument call site (33 of this mod's 35) and quietly changes behaviour;
# only the two BlockPos sites fail, because absSnapTo has no BlockPos/Vec3 overload.
# X7: a member rename must name its owner.  A bare member:moveTo also rewrites
# PathNavigation.moveTo(x,y,z,speed), which is a DIFFERENT method that 26.2 did not
# rename -- caught because the resulting snapTo(x,y,z,double) matched no overload.  A
# navigation call that happened to have a compatible arity would have compiled.
re:(?<!Navigation\(\))\.moveTo\(
re:\.absMoveTo\(
re:\.absRotateTo\(
# ServerPlayer.serverLevel() folded into level(), which is covariant on ServerPlayer.
re:\.serverLevel\(
# -- REGEX rules: differences that are not a token swap.
# Level.isClientSide became a private field with a public accessor. Only field reads
# need the (); a call that is already isClientSide() must not become isClientSide()().
re:\.isClientSide\b(?!\s*\()

# -- EntityType.Builder.build(String) became build(ResourceKey<EntityType<?>>) (the
# -- 1.21.2 change this project's migrator catalog records as M4). Written fully
# -- qualified on purpose: a rewrite that needed three new imports per file would have
# -- to edit import blocks, and this table only ever rewrites expressions.
# -- GameRules was overhauled: constants lost the RULE_ prefix, are typed GameRule<T>,
# -- and their serialized ids changed too (advance_time / spawn_mobs, not the old
# -- camelCase doDaylightCycle / doMobSpawning). Verified by reading each field's
# -- registerBoolean("<id>", ...) call out of the static initialiser, not by name
# -- resemblance. (The mod this was measured on references no gamerule ids as strings, so only the constants move.)
re:GameRules\.RULE_DAYLIGHT\b
re:GameRules\.RULE_DOMOBSPAWNING\b
re:GameRules\.RULE_WEATHER_CYCLE\b
# -- ResourceKey.location() -> identifier(), following ResourceLocation -> Identifier.
# ⚠ MUST require the PARENTHESES. As a bare `member:location` this eats a FIELD named
#    `location` -- which for a Minecraft mod is a very likely field name, and one config library has
#    exactly one (`ImageTitle.this.location`, a texture id). It compiled as `this.identifier`
#    and failed with `cannot find symbol: variable identifier`, which reads like a missing
#    vanilla member rather than a rule that over-reached. A space mod has two such sites and
#    escaped only because both live in files it OVERLAYS on 26.2 -- luck, not design.
#    This is X7 ("a member rename must name its owner") with a second clause: a rename for a
#    METHOD must also require the call syntax, or it silently rewrites same-named fields.
re:\.location\(\)
# -- Minecraft.setScreen -> setScreenAndShow.
re:\.setScreen\(
# -- Player.displayClientMessage(text, actionBar) split into sendOverlayMessage(text) and
# -- sendSystemMessage(text), so the boolean now picks a METHOD and there is no rename that
# -- works. Routed through a per-version compat helper instead; every receiver in this mod
# -- is a simple identifier or a.b (checked), so the call site rewrite is safe. Written
# -- fully qualified so no import has to be added.
# -- so both targets route through a compat helper. The get pattern requires an ARGUMENT so
# -- 26.x NBT accessors return Optional; the *Or forms preserve 1.21.1 semantics exactly
# -- (the old getInt returned 0 when the key was absent, which is what getIntOr(k, 0) does).
# -- Each pattern excludes any call containing a comma, so a two-argument call on a DIFFERENT
# -- type is never touched -- Brigadier's StringArgumentType.getString(ctx, "name") being the
# -- one that would otherwise be silently mangled. Written for the whole accessor
# -- family defensively, so an unused member is expected rather than a bug.
re:\.getString\(([^,()]+)\)
re:(?<!Boolean)\.getBoolean\(("[^"]*")\)
re:\.getDouble\(([^,()]+)\)
re:\.getCompound\(([^,()]+)\)
# getList lost its element-type argument; both arities collapse to getListOrEmpty.
# The single-arg form has no call site in this mod today; it is kept as coverage of the
# documented change rather than deleted, so it is marked rather than left to look dead.
# -- CompoundTag.getUUID/putUUID have no 26.x equivalent (a UUID goes through a codec now),
# -- so both targets route through a compat helper. The get pattern requires an ARGUMENT so
# -- it cannot touch the 50 no-arg Entity.getUUID() calls, which are unrelated and fine.
# -- 26.x collapsed the three interaction-result types into one InteractionResult.
# -- The Holder forms carried a payload (the resulting ItemStack) that the new API does not
# -- take, so the argument is dropped -- vanilla now reads the stack back from the player.
re:InteractionResultHolder\.success\([^;]*\)
re:InteractionResultHolder\.pass\([^;]*\)
re:InteractionResultHolder\.fail\([^;]*\)
re:InteractionResultHolder\.consume\([^;]*\)
# NOTE, behavioural: 1.21.1's sidedSuccess(x, isClientSide) meant "SUCCESS on the client, CONSUME on the
# server". 26.x folds that decision into SUCCESS itself, so this is the faithful mapping --
# but it is the one rule here that is a judgement rather than a pure rename, so it is worth
# eyeballing in-game (the arm-swing on use) rather than trusting the compile.
re:InteractionResultHolder\.sidedSuccess\([^;]*\)
net.minecraft.world.InteractionResultHolder
re:InteractionResultHolder<[^>]*>
# -- ItemInteractionResult likewise folds in. PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION is exactly
# -- what TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND now expresses.
ItemInteractionResult.PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION
net.minecraft.world.ItemInteractionResult
ItemInteractionResult

# -- CLIENT RENDERING: the render-state split.
# -- 26.x threads a render state through EntityRenderer<T, S>, and GeckoLib 5 follows with
# -- GeoEntityRenderer<T, R>. Only the ARITY changes for this mod: GeckoLib 5 keeps the
# -- (Context, GeoModel<T>) constructor, and it mixes GeoRenderState into vanilla's
# -- EntityRenderState (client.EntityRenderStateMixin), so any vanilla state satisfies R.
# -- All six of this mod's GeckoLib renderers draw living entities (Mob / PathfinderMob /
# -- Illusioner / Rabbit), so LivingEntityRenderState is the right state for every one.
re:extends GeoEntityRenderer<([A-Za-z0-9_]+)>
# Every row below was resolved with `javap` / tools/find-member-26.py against
# build/moddev/artifacts/minecraft-patched-26.2.0.75-merged.jar, never from memory. §V's own history
# is the reason: a plausible cause fitted to one observation was wrong there too.
# -- EntityType's 158 constants moved to a NEW `EntityTypes` holder class, exactly as Blocks/Items
# -- are laid out. `EntityType` itself keeps only 2 statics, so the class stays, and only the
# -- constant references move. Written FULLY QUALIFIED (§V19): a table that rewrites expressions
# -- cannot add the import a bare `EntityTypes.X` would need.
re:(?<![\w.])EntityType\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)\b
# -- MobEffects took the names players actually use. Verified: the Holder<MobEffect> constants are
# -- SPEED / SLOWNESS / RESISTANCE, and the old names are absent from MobEffects.
# ⚠ ANCHORED ON THE OWNER, and the first cut was not, which broke 16 call sites. A bare
# -- `member:MOVEMENT_SPEED` also rewrites `Attributes.MOVEMENT_SPEED` -- and Attributes STILL HAS
# -- that constant in 26.2, unchanged. The rule compiled the rename it was asked for and silently
# -- corrupted an unrelated class that happens to share a member name. It only surfaced because the
# -- error count went the wrong way on that family; a rule that had merely made an existing error
# -- LOOK different would have hidden it entirely.
# -- The general form, for the next row: a MEMBER rename must name its owner unless the member name
# -- is globally unique. Check with `javap <the other likely owner>` before using a bare member rule.
re:\bMobEffects\.MOVEMENT_SPEED\b
re:\bMobEffects\.MOVEMENT_SLOWDOWN\b
re:\bMobEffects\.DAMAGE_RESISTANCE\b
re:\bMobEffects\.DAMAGE_BOOST\b
re:\bMobEffects\.DIG_SPEED\b
re:\bMobEffects\.JUMP\b
# -- §M's M2 rename, arriving here from the other direction: on 26.2 `Registry.get(rl)` returns
# -- Optional<Holder.Reference<T>> and the plain-value lookup is `getValue`. Anchored on the ONE
# -- registry receiver this repo actually uses, so it cannot touch Map.get/Optional.get. (A second
# -- rule for `registryAccess().lookupOrThrow(..).get(` was written and the dead-rule detector
# -- rejected it: that shape does not occur here. §X1 -- an unfired rule is indistinguishable from
# -- an unneeded one unless something counts.)
re:\b(BuiltInRegistries\.[A-Z_]+)\.get\(
# -- Level.random is protected now; the accessor was always there. ANCHORED ON THE RECEIVER, and
# -- that anchoring is the whole point (§X7): this row was `re:\.random\.next` for one tree in which
# -- nothing declared a field of its own named `random`. In the next tree it silently rewrote
# -- `this.random.nextInt(...)` inside an Entity/Particle subclass -- where `random` is still a
# -- perfectly good `protected final` field -- into `this.getRandom()`, which Particle does not have.
# -- Entity.random and Particle.random are BOTH still protected+accessible on 26.2 (checked with
# -- javap); only Level.random needs the accessor, so only a level-shaped receiver may be rewritten.
re:(\w*[Ll]evel(?:\(\))?)\.random\b
# ⚠ JUDGEMENT ROW, not a rename — read before trusting it (§W6).
# getMinBuildHeight/getMaxBuildHeight became getMinY/getMaxY, and the SEMANTICS CHANGED:
# 1.21.1's getMaxBuildHeight() was EXCLUSIVE (minY + height); 26.2's getMaxY() is INCLUSIVE
# (bytecode: getMinY + getHeight - 1). A straight rename compiles perfectly and silently shortens
# every loop by one block. The `+ 1` restores the old meaning; a NEW loop should prefer <= getMaxY().
re:\.getMinBuildHeight\(
re:\.getMaxBuildHeight\(\)
# -- Permissions, part 2: the two shapes the LEVEL_GAMEMASTERS row above does not reach.
# (a) A COMPOUND requires-predicate. `Commands.hasPermission(check)` returns a
#     PermissionProviderCheck, which `implements Predicate<T>` — so the extra condition composes

# Read out of OnlyInWarningsHandler's bytecode rather than assumed: it opens with
# `if (FMLEnvironment.isProduction()) return;`, then scans the mod file's whole annotation set
# for net.neoforged.api.distmarker.OnlyIn and raises `loadwarning.neoforge.onlyin` if it finds
# ANY. So a SHIPPED jar is inert and a player never sees it -- but every gate here runs in DEV,
# where it is fatal on a dedicated server (Gate B dies before a test runs) and puts NeoForge's
# LoadingErrorScreen up on a client, which §X16 records stalling a whole Gate C run.

# (§X23), and one with any should not have to discover this. `[^)]*` matches newlines, which is
